utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, Madam Registrar. Could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-03-68-T, the Prosecutor versus Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam. Mr. Oric, can you follow the proceedings in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours, ladies and gentlemen, I can follow the proceedings in my own language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you may sit down. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour, Joanne Richardson on behalf of the Office of the Prosecution, making introductions to say -- this morning for Mr. Wubben who is unable to join us on -- during this morning's sessions. I also say good morning to our learned colleagues from the Defence. Joining me this morning is Mr. Gramsci di Fazio who will continue -- who will start his cross-examination, and also joining us this morning, Your Honour, is our case manager, Donnica Henry-Frijlink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam and good morning to you and your team. Appearances for Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. My name is Vasvija Vidovic. Together with Mr. John Jones I appear for Mr. Naser Oric. We have with us our legal assistant, Ms. Adisa Mehic, and our CaseMap manager, Mr. Geoff Roberts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam and good morning to you and your team. Can we bring in the witness? Any preliminaries? Okay. One thing I wanted to -- in the meantime, usher, you can please proceed. There is in the latest or most recent filing on Rule 68, which is the Defence response, there is a new allegation, a fresh allegation, or an allegation of a fresh violation, a new violation of Rule 68. We were intending to come down with a decision very early next week, that means Monday, on all the pending issues on Rule 68 and we would appreciate if you could either respond verbally, if we will have time today. If not, to file a short response on that new allegation by the end of business today so that then when we meet on Monday the three judges prefer to discuss this matter and incorporate our deliberations and decisions in our decision. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Today we'll have one break, that's at quarter to 11, of half an hour, and then we'll finish at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, sir. We are going to proceed with the last few questions by Madam Vidovic and then we will start with the cross-examination. Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Examined by Ms. Vidovic: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we move back into private session where we left it off yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's go back to private session. You have no opposition to be in private session on this matter, Mr. Di Fazio? MR. DI FAZIO: No, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I thank you so much, Madam Vidovic. So good morning to you, Mr. Smajlovic. Now that the examination-in-chief is over, the Prosecution takes over with its cross-examination. Your responsibility is the same here. You need to answer all the questions that are put to you truthfully and I suggest that you also keep answering in a short, concise, and to-the-point manner. Mr. Di Fazio will be cross-examining you. I don't know if we will finish today. It's not likely that we do, which basically means that you will be here over the weekend and then we'll finish with you on Monday, for sure. If you haven't made arrangements already through the V and W section of our Tribunal to advise your family that you will be staying over in The Hague, please let me know and I'll make sure that they are contacted immediately. So Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Your Honours. Cross-examined by Mr. Di Fazio:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Smajlovic.

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know my name. I've got some questions for you. The nickname Soson was a nickname that you had in 1992 as well, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From January 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There must be some misunderstanding, I think. You just told us that you had -- your nickname is Soson, that you had that nickname in 1992, didn't you? You had it all your life, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, that nickname has several meanings and varieties. Soson, Sole, Soso.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know that anyone else in -- from your village and from the Srebrenica area who also had the nickname Soson, or are you the only person it would had that nickname, as far as you're aware?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was the only person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What does it mean exactly? I mean, because he said it had several meanings. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you answer His Honour's question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Why out of all the possible nicknames that they could have given you they chose this one for you, Soson?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, Your Honours, I did not understand your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You did not choose this nickname yourself. It was chosen for you by your friends, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Sole, this nickname, was given to me by my aunt who lives in America. When I was born she was in Bosnia and she gave me this nickname Sole because that name is known in America and they use it in that part of America where she lived. It is a strange name in our area and my mother accepted that name but she also gave me my real name, Suad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. It's more or less what happened to me. I was born and christened with one name and then immediately after I was never called by it. So let's proceed. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said in evidence when you -- on the first day that you testified that you were the assistant commander for security in the 282nd Brigade. When did you obtain that position? I know it was after the fall of Srebrenica, but at what particular point of time?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was my wartime assignment in 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you remember when in 1994 you received that appointment or position?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 10th of January 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that when you became a member of the army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That was when I was given my wartime assignment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you become a member of the army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I arrived in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when was that? Was that in 1997?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, who employed you, who were you working for, from the 10th of January 1994 as assistant commander for security in the 282nd Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just told you that I received my wartime assignment. This was just on the paper. I did not work for anyone. I did not have any duties or did not hold any post.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you received some piece of paper or assignment to become assistant commander for security but that was utterly hollow, it meant nothing, it translated into no action, you had no duties, no responsibilities in that regard. Do I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What's the problem, Ms. Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness did not say that he received a piece of paper.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I did not say that. I did not say that I received any paper, any orders, any appointment. I was simply told at that time this fact. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Piece of paper or?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exactly. I can quite understand Madam Vidovic's intervention but, at the same time, what he had said earlier certainly now needs clarification. He said "I just told you that I received my wartime assignment. This was just on paper. I did not work for anyone. I did not have any duties or did not hold any post." So if it was on paper, which paper are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I did not say "task." I said "assignment." Assignment is something else in this context.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Who gave you this assignment? Who communicated it to you? I'm sorry to butt in. MR. DI FAZIO: No, no, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But I think it needs to be clear. Because it doesn't work for heaven. I mean, someone must have told you, "Suad, this is what you're going to do during the war."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's not what I was told. I was told that I was given an assignment within an establishment on paper, I would be the assistant commander for security. I never received any instructions, tasks or the job description.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have to apologise but I have to intervene. There is a misunderstanding because the interpreter keeps saying the word "imenovanje", keeps saying the word "zadatak" instead of "imenovanje." So that's a misinterpretation. In fact, the witness is using the word rasporad, assignment, and the interpreter uses another term in B/C/S which can be translated as "task."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. It will take me at least three days with my limited intelligence to understand the difference between task and assignment, but let's proceed. I think we can proceed and forget whether it's a piece of paper or not. It's still not clear in my minds who told him. MR. DI FAZIO: No. I would like to be clear about that if I could proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't care how you were told, whether it was by a piece of paper or a conversation in a cafe or smoke signals. All I want to know is: How did you become aware that you had received this assignment or tasking or job? How did you become aware of it?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I learned about it from my commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which commander? What was his name?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ibro Dudic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was he a commander in the army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He had also been given his wartime assignment as the commander of the Brigade where I had been assigned as -- that was my wartime assignment, and one of his tasks was to inform all of us about those assignments or appointments that is we had received.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You would agree with me, wouldn't you, that this assignment or tasking was a hollow one in that it meant in practical terms nothing? You didn't do anything that might be remotely construed as being an assistant commander for security. You did nothing that -- to carry out such a task?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did nothing and the other people who had received their wartime assignments, they did nothing either, because the place was demilitarised at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And the same applies to Mr. Ibro Dudic, your commander? He did nothing?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He did nothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were informed of this by Mr. Ibro Dudic, what did you say? Did you inform him that it came to you as a surprise that you were being appointed as assistant commander for security even though it was a meaningless assignment?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He merely invited us and told us that we had been given wartime assignments, that we would not be doing anything, and that's all there was to it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you express any surprise at this assignment that had landed in your lap? You hadn't sought it, I take it.

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was surprised.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you question Mr. Dudic and say, "I have no idea what you're talking about. Why am I a being appointed as assistant commander for security in the 282nd Brigade?" Did you query him?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We did not go into any details.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time you were informed, of course, you didn't know that it was an empty task in the sense that you wouldn't actually be doing anything, did you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes? Mr. Jones?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, well Your Honour this whole line of questioning is clearly intended to make it sound as if there is something ridiculous in this situation. The witness has explained the area was demilitarised and that's why he understood the situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Stop, please. Please. Please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Jones you may not. Please, when I say stop, stop. You're hinting at the witness, you're suggesting to the witness the way he should interpret and answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'm not hinting or suggesting anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jones, please sit down. Sit down. When I say stop, stop. Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you received this tasking or assignment, did you query him as to what you would be required to do?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not ask him anything. Let me repeat. At that time, the place was demilitarised. We did not have any weapons. We did not have anything. We were civilians. Everything had been taken away from us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You see, Mr. Jones, now?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness explained --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I hope you will not do that again because --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness explained --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- you will be punished, you will be severely punished and reprimanded by this Trial Chamber if you do that again, you or Ms. Vidovic or anyone from the Prosecution side. I will not tolerate if. This is abusing of the process in the worst manner possible and it's very unethical, Mr. Jones, especially from someone who's coming from the kind of reputable jurisdiction that you do.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness already answered that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Jones, you clearly suggested to the witness the way he should deal with Mr. Di Fazio's question. What is your problem, Ms. Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, please look at the transcript just a few lines before the intervention by my colleague, Mr. Jones. You will clearly see that the witness replied that this was the time when the place was demilitarised. Please have a look at the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. But it's still -- then that was followed by another question and that's when Mr. Jones intervened and he suggested the way the witness should answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The incident is finished Madam Vidovic. Please sit down and let's proceed with the questions. MR. DI FAZIO: I'll proceed, if Your Honours please. In fact, I'll move away from the topic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1997 you became a professional soldier in the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In the federation army, not in the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You conducted extensive training, including training overseas, I think?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the course of your training as a soldier, you became aware, didn't you, of the principle of subordination, what is called the principle of subordination?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the course of your training as a soldier from 1997 onwards, did you become familiar with the principle of subordination, the notion that you must follow orders, that the commanders are responsible for the actions of their troops, the existence of chains of command?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did those principles of subordination exist in the army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina in 1992 and 1993? Do you know that? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was not in existence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, what was not in existence, the army or those principles of subordination, or you don't know?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The principles of subordination did not exist. Let me stress that the conditions were not there. No staffs had been established. I have already said the conditions were not there for any staffs to be established. If you want to have staffs you need logistics, communications equipment, uniforms, equipment, barracks, professionals, ranks, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Apart from the area of Srebrenica, do you know - if you don't know tell us - but apart from the area of Srebrenica, and other parts of the Republic of Bosnia, as far as you're aware, did the army operate utilising the principles of subordination? Not the VRS, I mean; I mean the Muslim army.

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. It's possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like the Prosecutor to place his questions in -- within a specific time frame work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please do, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Sorry. I was talking about 1992 and 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But I'll -- does that clarify the question for you?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not understand you. What do you mean 1992, 1993?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as you're aware, did the principles of subordination apply in the Muslim army in 1992 and 1993? Outside of the area surrounding Srebrenica. Apart from the area around Srebrenica. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Finally, in 1992 and 1993, did any elements of the army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina operate at all in Srebrenica or in the area immediately around Srebrenica, including your -- Kazani and all the areas that you saw and went to and fought in, in 1992 and 1993? Were any army elements there at all?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Those were local groups that were operating in those areas.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I did not want to interrupt the questions asked by Mr. Di Fazio. I wish he would stop calling the BH army "Muslim army" outside of Srebrenica because that's not what it is, what it was. Bosnia and Herzegovinian army is something quite different from a Muslim army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Again, I object to this kind of objection. You should have asked the Trial Chamber to send the witness out to make a submission and we would have sent the witness out and you would have made -- you would have had all the opportunity to make the submission. This way you have told the witness what your position is with regard this matter and how he should respond if he is asked questions referring to the Muslim army.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, no, because -- not at all. The witness had already answered the question. His answer is complete.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What you said is tantamount to a submission, Ms. Vidovic and submissions should not be made in the presence of the witnesses. Let's proceed, Mr. Di Fazio. I cooperate with both of you. Whenever you want to make a submission, even it takes one hour, I will send the witness out, explain to him that we need to deal with something which has got nothing to do with him or her, whoever that be, and I will give you all the opportunity. But please try to avoid making submissions, even if -- sometimes it does not occur to one's mind that it may be a submission. But to us it's clearly a submission. Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Could we have the witness out, please, Your Honour because this is really a critical --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please send the witness out, please. Mr. Smajlovic we will be coming back to you very soon. We need to discuss something. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I for one, Your Honour, I really trust Your Honour will actually hear me out and allow me to make this submission because Your Honour has just accused me of some extremely serious professional breaches of ethics, which is an extremely grave matter for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And there is more to come, Mr. Jones. Because we have still not forgotten, although you think you did not commit any grave misdemeanour here, when you called Mr. Wubben the high priest of surprises in the context of ambushes that we were talking about at the time, you did commit a grave -- and you haven't come back with a direct apology to Mr. Wubben. As yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I say two -- may I first of all reply to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is not the first time, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour I opened by asking whether I could actually -- whether Your Honour would hear me out. I'm not sure if I'm being given the right to be heard out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, oh, no, yes, of course not. You have never been given the right to be heard, Mr Jones. You have I have every reason to complain and everyone will take you seriously if you do.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, am I able to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jones, please don't use these tactics with me. We have never shut you down. We have always given you all the opportunities to say what you like even when you were saying things that you knew yourself were not valid. So please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, for the first matter I have been asked for the most basic right to be heard out and I hope I'll be able to finish without -- without being interrupted. You've mentioned again this matter of allegedly a grave misdemeanour of calling Mr. Wubben something. I apologised on the very occasion. I immediately apologised. If -- I had no idea the matter --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Jones, Mr. Jones I didn't interrupt you because you never did apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I finish?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I have read through the transcript 100.000 times and you did not apologise. You even pretended - us - to agree with you that it was something which was not grave at all, if you look at the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, the word "apology" is there. I apologised and I apologise now unreservedly to Mr. Wubben and I trust the matter is therefore closed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That is better.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: May I trust that that matter is closed, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, now it is closed, yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. Now as far as --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- apologise to Mr. Wubben. We didn't want an apology to us without an apology to Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. Thank you, Your Honour. Now as far as today is concerned, and it's at page 14, line 14 to 16 of the transcript, the witness answered -- he was asked, "You did nothing to carry out such a task." He said, "No, I did" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Jones, I'm going to interrupt you. That platter is closed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, my reputation was attacked by Your Honour and I'm defending myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That matter is closed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So there is it no misbehaviour on my part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, that matter is closed. We said that that matter is closed and it's closed. Madam Vidovic tried to give that interpretation which you are now going to try and give again. That matter is closed. That was one question and the next question dealt with another aspect, and that's when you tried to suggest to the witness that he should still concentrate on the demilitarisation as the basis for his answer. So that matter is closed. Yes, we think you abused the process, Mr. Jones, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, then, I have to withdraw, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's proceed. Go ahead, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would ask you very kindly if you could make a break now at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We'll have a break of ten minutes. --- Break taken at 9.57 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Let's bring the witness in. And let me make it clear, we will not tolerate the least - the least - hint at arrogance here. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We will not allow anyone to be the least arrogant. You have both been treated in a manner which is almost incomparable to anything that one would expect in such a Tribunal. Yes, Madam Vidovic I saw you standing up.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I would only like that the treatment be equally accorded to us and the Prosecutor, the treatment accorded be equal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It has always been so. And what you're saying, you mean that it has not been equal, please stand up and say so now. We have been extremely patient, extremely patient allowing interventions simply due to ignorance of what the procedural rules ought -- the real procedural rules ought to apply in this Tribunal. We have been very, very, very patient. Yes, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Di Fazio: [Continued] MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's move on, Mr. Smajlovic, and I'd like to ask you some questions about the Bajramovici meeting, the little meeting that you told us about, that happened in Bajramovici. Can I ask you -- can I ask you this: Had your group, the Kazani group, or whatever its correct name is, been formed prior to the meeting?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean my group in Kazani? Is that what you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I just want to be clear about it. I think I'm clear but do I understand that all the other groups, or many of the other groups that eventually emerged in 1992 in the Srebrenica area, for example, Mr. Tursunovic's group, were they already formed at the time of the Bajramovici meeting? I'm talking about the meeting in May, the 20th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The groups, all of them, were set up at the time when their villages came under attack by the Serbs, or, rather, the Chetniks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That might have been the process but what I want to know is had they emerged as groups with identifiable leaders by the time of the Bajramovici meeting, the 20th of May? Was there already a Kazani group with you as its leader, a Suceska group with Mr. Tursunovic as its leader, and so on?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of them were; some of them weren't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So groups later emerged with identifiable leaders, later I mean after the 20th of May when the Bajramovici meeting occurred?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As I indicated a moment ago, the groups were set up at the time when the Chetniks started attacking their villages, when they were attempting to defend themselves. This meant that this was from the start of the aggression in Bosnia-Herzegovina, meaning from their first attempt to enter Srebrenica onwards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I've understood you. What I'm asking is this: Did groups emerge with leaders, local groups with leaders, for example, like yours, after the 20th of May Bajramovici meeting or had they already emerged or were they already identifiable and their leaders known? That's what I'm interested in.

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already answered this. Some of them existed, and even before the 20th of May 1992, whereas others emerged subsequently, depending on when their villages came under attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's what I wanted to know. Now, you -- I couldn't get the name from the transcript but I think the person you said who invited you to the meeting was a gentleman named Sefket Djorzic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He invited me to the meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did he -- did he explain what the purpose of the meeting was?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He didn't explain what the purpose of the meeting was, and I didn't know anything about it until we all gathered up there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know who was going to be there?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. I didn't know who was to attend the meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you go? Why --

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went over to see what was going to happen, because this was close to where my house was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You knew, didn't you, that it was going to concern at least the -- in some broad sense, the defence of the Muslim people in the area? You knew that at least, didn't you? Or am I wrong?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I presumed so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you speak to your men about any particular position or stance or view that you could adopt at the meeting regarding the defence of the Muslim people? In other words, what position you might adopt on any such issue at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. I've already told you, and I will repeat, at this meeting there was just discussion about what was happening to the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But I think you've told us that the -- that you presumed that the meeting was going to concern in some broad sense the defence of the Muslim people and your group was set up to precisely that reason, to defend the Muslim people. Is there any particular reason why you didn't consult with your group about what position to adopt on this very important issue?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never consulted with my group. I always took the decisions by myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, if we just diverge for a moment, when precisely was your group formed, approximately when, the Kazani group?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Around the 20th of April, or rather from the 20th of April onwards. I'm not sure that the 20th is the exact date. It may have been later, depending on who joined my group and when.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And within your particular group then you, is it fair to say, you tell me if I'm right or wrong, is it fair to say that you held quite some authority? You didn't have to consult with them and you were its commander?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was only a local leader, nothing more. They trusted me. Whenever we set out somewhere, they trusted me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that. You're a leader and it's local and it's a group. I understand that and I've got no problem with that. I understand what you're saying. But within this local group, you as its leader held quite some authority. You didn't have to consult with them, as you've said, about decisions that you took. Is that a fair assessment?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It is not. Although I sometimes made a decision that we ought to go somewhere, the people had their choice to decide whether to join or not. Nobody could force them to do something they didn't want to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. And on this particular occasion, when you were attending a meeting to decide how best to organise resistance, how best to defend the Muslim people, you didn't consult your group?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't consult them. There was no need for that, as I myself was unaware of what the discussion at the meeting would revolve around.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, but you weren't -- with respect, that's not actually what you've said, is it? You had an idea, didn't you, that the purpose of the meeting was to discuss the defence of the Muslim people? Isn't that correct? You may not have known the precise details but that was the basic topic. You knew that, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said that I presumed as much. Knowing and presuming are two different things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just want to ask you some general questions about the situation in Srebrenica and the outlying -- and the area in which you found yourself in 1992. You would agree with me, wouldn't you, that the -- that the Serb forces in the area posed a very dangerous threat to you? They were a dangerous and ruthless enemy, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were only very well armed and they had one sole purpose, to carry out ethnic cleansing of the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they also had, I think you would agree with me here, wouldn't you, that they had a superiority, a clear superiority in arms and military technology, the means with which to wage modern warfare, correct?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were well armed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whereas the Muslim forces, or the Bosniaks living in the area, including these local groups that emerged, they consisted of men who were inexperienced and ill-equipped; is that correct? Ill-equipped militarily?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The groups were armed with hunting rifles, makeshift rifles. They did not have uniforms. Therefore they wore civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it then that you'll agree with me that they were ill-equipped compared to the Serbs and inexperienced in the sense of not being formally trained?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We practically had no professional weaponry of the type the Serbs had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thinking back of your experiences in 1992 and early 1993, leading up to demilitarisation, and bringing to bear everything that you've learned as a professional soldier, would you agree with me that being able to gather and direct the few military resources that the Muslims had, the Bosniaks had, to deal with Serb threats would have been a desirable thing?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question? I haven't understood the last part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thinking back with everything that you saw and experienced back then in 1992 and early 1993, and also bearing in mind everything that you've learned as a soldier, professional soldier, would you agree with me that in the circumstances that existed at the time, it would have been desirable, a good thing, for you, the Bosniak forces, the Muslim forces, to gather -- to be able to gather together and direct the few military resources that you had to deal with threats, Serb threats, as and where they arose?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've been telling you that we only had some obsolete and damaged weapons that we managed to seize from the Serbs. That was all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And I've heard you and understood you, and what I'm saying to you is, in those circumstances, in precisely those circumstances that you just described, don't you agree that it would have been desirable back in 1992 for you and the other local groups to be able to gather and direct their few, their limited military resources, to deal with Serb threats as and where they arose? In other words, to be able to initiate military action, be able to concentrate fire-power, the limited fire-power that you had in hot spots, trouble spots, as and where they arose in the area?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I've understood your question, but I'll tell you again that the groups were independent of each other and nobody could take the weapons from a person who had captured the weapon in a different group. Besides, there were no conditions, there was no time, there was no space even for us to get organised that way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I've heard you and understood you, okay? There is no problem there. I understand, but -- and I know what you say. But thinking back, with the knowledge of hindsight, okay? Thinking back now, looking back on the situation, would you agree that it would have been a good idea to be able to gather and direct the few military resources that you had in order to -- and to be able to initiate military action and concentrate fire-power in order to deal with Serb -- with the Serbs, as and when they created problems in the Srebrenica area?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I reiterate that the groups operated independently and that the region of Srebrenica, including the surrounding villages, was cut off internally and there were no conditions in place for that, in order for us to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. At the meeting, you've given evidence that Mr. Oric was appointed as a coordinator, and he was responsible for coordinating matters between the military leaders, possibly other things, but certainly coordinating matters between the -- the local commands, I should say. You remember that evidence?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. I said that he coordinated on the ground among the leaders, and I wish to say the following: The leaders themselves could never agree on what they should do and how they should do it. I gave you an example that Hakija Meholjic and Akif Ustic could never agree on anything at a given point in time, about how to approach a certain matter. The same went for Hakija Meholjic and Zulfo Tursunovic. He wanted to balance out their relations, their mutual relations. At no point in time did I mean that he coordinated over something because coordination can be carried out in many different ways. Coordination is no military term. You can coordinate matters on a stadium between players there or matters in a school environment. At no point did the term body or the term coordination meaning that he had the role of a commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness answered -- the question concerned coordination between military commands, a matter that he never even mentioned. He spoke about group leaders. MR. DI FAZIO: If I said something about military commands, I apologise. My understanding is clear about what the witness has said and I understand absolutely the fact that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You said the local commands, as it is in the transcript, but I don't know if you said that or you said local commanders. I think you said the local commanders, if I remember well. MR. DI FAZIO: I apologise, and if I said local commands I didn't mean that in the slightest. I meant local leaders and, rest assured, Mr. Smajlovic, that I've understood your evidence concerning local leaders, okay?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the meeting at Bajramovici, was there any other model considered for resisting the Serbs? For example, creating a unified military command with chains of command so that a leader emerged who could issue orders and direct the forces that were available to deal with the Serb threat? Was that ever discussed?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was not discussed. As I've already said, this body could only make decisions by vote, no other way was envisaged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let's go to the actual meeting itself. It's held in Bajramovici and the local leaders, some -- some, I should say, sorry, some local leaders of local groups turned up. How did they know to attend the meeting? We know how you got there from the invitation from Mr. Djok -- from Sefket but how did the other leaders, local leaders, get there?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Messages were sent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whose idea was it to organise this meeting, do you know?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And -- okay. Do I take it that you didn't know at the time and you have never found out who it was that called this meeting?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This was not discussed at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was a big -- it was a very important event, wasn't it, for the local people, the Muslim -- the Bosniak people in the Srebrenica area, given all of the horrors that were starting to unfold? Extremely important matter, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I would not agree with you, because, had this meeting been very important only the group leaders would have attended not the women, the people who were there from that neighbourhood, from the houses in that neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who proposed the model of coordinator of local leaders and local groups, do you know?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We all proposed something or other so nobody said, "This is how it will be." I don't remember exactly somebody said the best thing will be to have a body, to elect a body. It doesn't matter who would be heading the body but let us do this by vote so that nobody can feel any rancor towards the others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was this -- was this particular proposal made by the local leaders or everyone else who had gathered there?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All those present there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the issue of coordination, was that -- was that discussed at length at the meeting and clearly defined and worked out?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Nothing was done in detail.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you press for perhaps some detail to be added to the proposal? Yourself, you personally. Did you suggest that perhaps you had to do something a little more given the situation that confronts us, that we have to have something more concrete?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not. The only discussion that I participated in and my only proposal was for to us help each other and to save our lives in the face of the impending attack by the aggressor who was already at the gates of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you walk away from the meeting knowing what sort of coordination Mr. Oric was going to conduct?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you just explain to us once again what the -- what precisely his role was and who explained it at the meeting? Who made clear what coordination actually entailed?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said yesterday that his role had been to coordinate among the leaders because the individual leaders could not agree, could not see eye to eye, and I said that if a group fought the Serbs, then another village, in order not to come under threat, we decided to also arrange this. So he was supposed to smooth things out among the leaders so that even those leaders who did not want to provide any help or did not have any interest in helping, that they would also lend a hand when needed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would you agree with me that in the circumstances, given the threats that you faced, this role of coordinator was really quite an important one?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't agree. He could go there and ask that person, then try to coordinate things, but nobody was bound to obey. If I wanted to go, I could have gone and it did not matter if the fact that he was there to coordinate things between me and the other leader, that wasn't really important.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If it wasn't really important and you could have done the job, can you offer any -- us any insight as to why it was necessary to have a coordinator in the first place?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I've already told you a little while ago, if a group was fighting the Serbs, in order to prevent any threats from spreading to another village, this was in order to attempt to make some kind of a balance and to get the others to help that group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, important or unimportant, for a coordinator to be able to carry out his job effectively it's important, isn't it, that he enjoy some confidence amongst the local leaders? Would you agree?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't agree.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So -- so the situation is you've got local leaders who are falling out with each other or can fall out from time to time, fall out with each other and disagree, correct? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you're surrounded by a ruthless Serb enemy who is intent on ethnic cleansing and is clearly superior in terms of arms, correct? I'm sure you can answer that with a yes or a no.

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the last part of your question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you and the other groups at Bajramovici, and the people who attended there and the people they represented, were surrounded by a ruthless Serb enemy who was intent on ethnic cleansing and clearly superior in terms of arms, correct?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was the -- the enemy was vastly superior in terms of arms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the local leaders were the only form of resistance to the Serbs that was available in the area at the time, correct?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The local leaders were that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in such circumstances, is it your evidence to the Trial Chamber that the job of coordinating these local leaders, who provided the only resistance to this ruthless enemy, was not so important? Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've told you. I've explained to you how important it was. He could not replace any of the local leaders, remove them from office. One example was when he tried to do that with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about appointments or dismissals of commanders. I'm not asking you about that. I'm asking you about the importance of the role of coordinator. You say -- I suggest -- I'll make it clear, okay? If things happened in the way you say they did, and I don't accept that, but if they did, then such a coordinator, such a man, carry out those positions in all of the circumstances would have had an absolutely fundamentally crucial role, absolutely fundamental role. Wouldn't you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree with you. He did not play a crucial role. Let me repeat. Independent leaders made their own decisions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. All right. At the outset of war -- sorry, not at the outset of war -- at the time of the meeting, Mr. Oric was quite a young man, wasn't he? I think you said 24 or 25, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was 24 or 25.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. He -- he didn't have any significant military knowledge, did he, according to you?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did not have any military knowledge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not only that but his -- the military service that everyone did in the former Yugoslavia made him particularly -- let me rephrase that. Not only that, but given his military training that he'd done, which was in nuclear, biological, and chemical defence, he really didn't have much at all in the terms of military experience according to you to be able to apply, to bring to bear, on the situation in which he and you found yourselves in, correct?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He did not have any military knowledge and based on his training in nuclear, biological, and chemical defence. So this training did not provide him with any military knowledge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he -- he wasn't popular either, was he, in the area? That's your evidence, correct?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He was not popular. I've already explained why. He had been Milosevic's escort at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He'd been seen on television, standing next to Mr. Milosevic, hadn't he?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You knew that at the time of the Bajramovici meeting, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he certainly -- I think you twice said that he held no particular -- in fact, twice you said that he was unpopular -- sorry, that he did not enjoy any popularity amongst the Muslim youth in the area. That's so, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was not popular among the Muslim youth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does it strike you as odd that a man who is unpopular, has no military experience, no relevant military experience, who has been seen on television standing next to Slobodan Milosevic, should get himself elected as -- or appointed as coordinator of local groups? Does that strike you as odd?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It's not odd. I can give you an example.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that meeting, I personally, and all the others present there, who were members of the young generation, and in fact I had some other reasons, Zulfo Tursunovic and Akif Ustic were older men and they kept quarrelling among them. And I myself said that Naser should be appointed because he was young, because we were in the same generation, we had been working together, and he had fought against the -- Arkan's men who had tried to enter Srebrenica. So the younger people sided with me. It would be easier to agree with younger people, a younger man, because the older people always had other issues, more issues, than we, the younger people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We need to have a break of 30 minutes now. Mr. Di Fazio, we'll reconvene at 11.20.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I see Mr. Wubben. Yes, now what do you have, Mr. Wubben?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I apologise, but for the record, Your Honour, I'm happy to join the team again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think so are we. We can't tell you how much. Let's continue. Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Thanks, Your Honours. Your Honours, I think I could probably give you a very brief, one- or two-minute reply to the new matters in the motion. If we do they in the reply -- you remember earlier this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: I don't propose to do it now but I just read it and, if Your Honours are thinking about the part of the reply that deals with additional Rule 68 matter, I think I can just say something about it and that would complete everything we want.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I suggest we stop five minutes, would five minutes suffice? MR. DI FAZIO: We'll be finishing at 1.00?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: At 1.00, yes. So we will stop five minutes before with this witness. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Let's proceed, and at the end of the sitting make sure that there is liaison, Mr. Wubben, and Madam, with the Defence as regards the major Dudley, in other words as per our decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Yes, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't want to spend too much time on the topic of the appointment of Mr. Oric, Mr. Smajlovic. Just before the break, you said that -- I was putting to you that it was odd that a man with Mr. Oric's background would be appointed as coordinator and you said, no, you -- assisted him or, rather, took the view that he would be a good appointment and you represented the younger generation. Did you mean by that that his -- he was supported at the meeting by younger local leaders?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That's not what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Sorry. Then I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. I read from his answer, page 38, lines 18, 19, 20, that's the area. His answer: "And I myself said that Naser should be appointed because he was young, because we were in the same generation, and we had been working together, and he had fought against Arkan's men who had tried to enter Srebrenica." This is the important part. So the younger people sided with me. This is what he said. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, thank you. That's what I recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So you just heard His Honour read out what you said. You supported Mr. Oric and the younger people supported you, sided with you, in taking a favourable view of the appointment of Mr. Oric as coordinator, correct?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But not all of these people were leaders. There were ordinary people there from the neighbourhood who attended the meeting as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine. How do you reconcile that with your evidence to Madam Vidovic on yesterday, Thursday, when she asked you question: You said that he appeared -- that he appeared toward the end of 1991. "Did he gather the Muslim youth around him? Was he a popular person among the young people?" And you answered, "No, he was not popular. At that time he was the personal escort of Slobodan Milosevic, Milosevic was a symbol of Serbdom and we would see him quite often on TV. He was standing right beside Milosevic." So I understood that yesterday he was saying that he wasn't popular and that included amongst young people. You seem to be saying something different. I'm putting to you that you're saying something different. Am I correct or not?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that he was not popular at that time. However, with the attacks and the crimes committed by the Serbs at the very beginning of the war, and with their advance towards Srebrenica, people regarded themselves as Muslims and not in terms of what they had been before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You mentioned I think earlier this morning, that one of the -- one of the reasons he was elected had been his exploits with Arkan or Arkan's men, I should say, earlier. Are you saying that played a part in the fact that he was appointed coordinator of the local groups?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps this played a part in it too, but the most important part of it was that he was Muslim, a member of the same peoples who were under the attack by the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I understand that. But just the fact that he was Muslim didn't have a particular -- that wasn't the specific reason that he was successful in being made coordinator of the local groups, was it? It wasn't just that.

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't understood. Can you repeat, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will repeat my question. Is the fact that he had dealt with Arkan or Arkan's men earlier, before the Bajramovici meeting on the 20th of May, did that play in your opinion or your view a part in his appointment as coordinator of local groups? Did that help him get the position, so to speak?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My answer was perhaps it did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it mentioned at the Bajramovici meeting? Did anyone say, "Mr. Oric, he's the man who dealt with Arkan's men" or words to that effect. "He should be local coordinator."

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Nothing was mentioned to that effect. These were only comments we made.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of Mr. Oric ever having had any experience in Kosovo, military experience?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm not aware of that. But I'm sure he did not have any such experience. He was a police officer there, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were shown various documents yesterday that, broadly speaking, dealt with or suggested that Mr. Oric was appointed commander of the Srebrenica TO, in particular they were P73 and P75. Isn't it the case that at the Bajramovici meeting he was appointed or elected or chosen as the commander of the Srebrenica TO?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I've said so and I repeat, he was merely a coordinator among the leaders. As for what is written on paper, anyone could have written that and I believe this was written in Sarajevo or in Tuzla, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And that was understood amongst everyone in the Srebrenica area, that Mr. Oric -- and I'm talking about 1992 and early 1993, leading up to demilitarisation. It was understood that Mr. Oric was no commander, that there was no commander of the local groups, that there was no commander of Muslim resistance; that was clearly understood in the community, correct or not?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you, all the leaders operated independently, locally, in the area, and they did not know --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yeah. What I'm saying is that as far as you're aware there was no perception amongst people in Srebrenica or the area around Srebrenica that Mr. Oric was the commander of local leaders, local groups, there was no perception, everyone understood that, that was clear?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was no such perception. He was just a group leader Potocari. That was all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think we understand each other. Okay. In later years, in 1993 or 1994, would there have been any reason that you can think of for people to have the perception that Mr. Oric was the commander of Bosniak forces or Bosniak groups operating in Srebrenica and the area around Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1993, no. There were no appointments or assignments to any duties. I repeat that as of the 10th of January 1994, there was -- there existed a wartime assignment, and people received their respective wartime assignments in that period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I would just like to you look at a video clip. MR. DI FAZIO: Would Your Honours just bear with me? Yes it's Exhibit P431. It's known to Your Honours as I think the anniversary speech. Can we just play that, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you look at this video clip and follow it, please?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "The Srebrenica municipal assembly cultural centre and the Srebrenica folklore club. I'm inviting the operations group commander Mr. Naser Oric to open. "Before I start I would like to greet all the president who wish a happy Kuban Bajram to the troops and people. "Dear guest, officers, and soldiers, we've gathered here today to honour the anniversary of the Srebrenica Territorial Defence staff." MR. Di FAZIO: Can I just interrupt the viewing there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can I ask you did you ever hear in 1992 or 1993 of something called the Srebrenica Territorial Defence staff? Have you ever heard of that body?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The staff of the territorial -- can you just repeat, please? Whether I ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever heard of a body called the Srebrenica Territorial Defence staff? Have you ever heard of them? Have you ever heard of it?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Srebrenica, no. I didn't. There were local groups operating in their respective areas as best they could. There was no Territorial Defence and no staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just incidentally, Mr. Smajlovic, while we are we, for the remainder of today and perhaps Monday, let me assure you that you have understood perfectly well your evidence concerning the local leaders and -- although I don't agree with it, I understand what you're saying very, very, very well, okay? So just to assure you about that. Now, let's just continue, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Of the Srebrenica armed forces and a brand new formational command the operations group of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina in the formation of the 2nd Corps. Gatherings like this one always give us the chance to remind ourselves of the very beginning of the war. Exactly 25 months ago the people in Eastern Bosnia fell into the clutches of the combatants of the new fascist wave founded on the still-existing barbarism in the middle of Europe. Our 25-month-long story and I don't know for how much longer it will go on about the misfortunes of this Muslim Bosniak people cannot be told during a meeting of this kind. That [unintelligible] of historic science and this time I hope without a demagogic approach. But let me remind of the inception of the Srebrenica Territorial Defence staff two years ago on this day. The appearance of leaders, the success of party leaders then, unarmed Muslims people started off a defensive war beyond the living memory and [unintelligible] organised in such a way the first combat started on the 20th of April 1992 in Potocari. And then came the first and second of May 1992. The defence of [unintelligible] 5th, 6th, and 7th of May". MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Bearing in mind what Mr. Oric -- let me withdraw that question. You would agree with me, wouldn't you, that Mr. Oric is as well placed as you are to comment on the emergence of organisations for the defence of the Muslim people in Srebrenica and the area around Srebrenica. Would you agree with that comment? He's as good a historian as you could be because he was there, he lived through it?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was on the front line together with his group, as a local leader, throughout the period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But you agree with me, don't you, that he is as well-placed as you are to be able to comment on the -- any organisations that emerged, that were dealing -- that were responsible for the defence of the Muslim people? You would agree with that or not? He certainly knew about his role as coordinator of local groups, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did not necessarily have to know what was going on at all points in time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We will deal with this quickly. Having heard what Mr. Oric has said so far on this video clip I showed you, and would you agree with me that there -- a Srebrenica TO did emerge at Bajramovici in May of 1992 and that he was a commander of it, Mr. Oric?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I wouldn't agree. Oric was appointed a commander in the course of 1994 on paper. He received his wartime assignment roster just as I did. He was given assignment as commander, just as I was given assignment as assistant commander for security. This was only on paper. I repeat that this was the periods of demilitarisation. There was no army there, only civilians. MR. DI FAZIO: I think I've finished with the clip. I don't need to go on with that any more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Judge Eser?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Just a matter of clarification, since we always have problems with translation of terms, could perhaps the witness asked whether the Serbo-Croat term for Srebrenica Territorial Defence, if he does know this term and if this term already existed at the time of 1992. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: His Honour's question is evident. Had you ever heard of the term, Srebrenica TO? Is that a term that is familiar to you? Srebrenica Territorial Defence. Is that a term that you are aware of?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was never mentioned. The term Territorial Defence was never used.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you've never heard it being used at all? It's not a term that you're familiar with? Do I understand you correctly or not?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The term itself, Territorial Defence, yes, but now if you're asking me whether it was mentioned or whether the establishment of the Territorial Defence was talked about, that never was the case in Srebrenica until 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think that's clear enough. Thank you. I'd like to show you some -- a document or two, please. I'd like to show you documents bearing ERN, range 01837894 to 97. Now, Mr. Smajlovic, this document or documents consists of two documents, one appears to be an application form consisting of one, two, three pages in B/C/S, and another page apparently signed by Mr. Oric. I would like you to first to look at the three page application form. That's your application. That's your document, isn't it, with your handwriting on it?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is not my handwriting. This is the first time that I see this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can -- I can explain, sir. You can see several different hand handwritings in this document. Also if you look at the education --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go through it in a bit more detail. Let's start at the top. First of all, there is a unique number of citizen. You see that, all those numbers there? Do you know what that number is?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is the ID number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it your ID number or was it your ID number back then in 1994?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's my number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your father's name is indeed Avdo and your mother's name, maiden name was Fadila Salihovic?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you already told us about your nickname. What about the date of birth? That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about item 16, which deals with your working years? Are those details of employment and -- yes, and -- yes, are those details of employment correct?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is not correct. First of all, you can see a different handwriting here, and in 1990 I joined the reserve police force, and then, after that, I became an active duty police officer and I remained an active-duty police officer until the beginning of the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And under item 29, there are details of your family. We don't need to mention them. But are those family details correct, names and dates of birth?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then -- well, let's go right to the end of the document. Is that your signature there or not?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is not my signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And are the details under item 40, namely the date of engagement in the RBiH army and the answer there being 20th of April 1992, commander of Company Kazani from 12th of July 1992, are those details correct?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The 20th of April, but as the group leader, not the company commander or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just pausing there, what happened on the 20th of April? What is the significance of that date in relation to your -- the Kazani group, is that the date of your election as leader or is it some other significance?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That is not the election as leader, but on that day, in the morning, strong Serb forces attacked the village of Kazani from the direction of Zalazje. First they started shelling the village and then they carried out an infantry attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And -- okay. Look, what I'm -- earlier, moments ago, I asked you about the date in item 41, the 20th of April, and I asked you about whether the details were correct and you said, "Yes, the 20th of April is correct." And then I asked you about the significance of the 20th of April, and then you told us about a Serb attack. Now, I'm trying to understand you as best I can. Am I correct that on the 20th of April there was a Serb attack and that therefore a group, like the Kazani group, was formed on the 20th of April and you were made its leader? I don't want to put words in your mouth but is my understanding correct?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not made a leader on that day; I became the leader as time went by. But that was the day when they attacked and when we offered resistance to the Chetniks who were attempting to enter the village of Kazani.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And was the Kazani group, of which you were leader, formed after the 20th of April in response to this attack?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, there was no organisation here, no gathering together. We simply all headed out to defend ourselves, and that is how the group came into being.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So your position is that this is the first time you've ever seen this document, you've never seen it before?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the first time. I only filled in a form in Tuzla on the 3rd of October 1997 when I became a professional soldier and active-duty serviceman in the federation army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you have no knowledge of anyone substituting -- sorry, completing this form and putting it through its -- whatever bureaucratic -- let me rephrase that. You have no knowledge of anyone completing this form on your behalf or with your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I have no knowledge of that. But I can see that the person who had filled this form in was not quite familiar with the dates, the situation, those elements.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that whoever did fill in the form had access to personal, quite personal details, for example, your nickname and the details about your family?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But anyone could have filled this in who had any contacts with my file at the police station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
